title: Prove you can recover
subtitle: Backups with custody, one rehearsed restore & the closing record
description: Close the Build path by proving the network can come back: scheduled directory and CA backups under ceremony-grade custody, policy, boundary, logs, and the living records in one hashed catalog, a timed restore rehearsal in isolation, and the recovery record that completes the Body of Evidence.
outcomes: Back up the directory, CA, policy, boundary, logs, and records into one verified catalog.
Rehearse a real system state restore in isolation, measured against written objectives.
File the tested-recovery record that completes the Body of Evidence for path 2.

stages.title: Decide what recovery must prove
stages.detail: Recovery starts as a list of promises: which systems and records must be restorable, how old a restored copy may be, how long restoration may take — written as commitments the rest of the course exists to keep.

stages.title: Back up the directory, on schedule
stages.detail: System state from both controllers, on a schedule, to the protected target — plus the quiet feature that handles the most common 'disaster' of all: the Recycle Bin for deleted directory objects.

stages.title: Back up the CA, policy, boundary, and records
stages.detail: The directory is not the only thing the network cannot re-derive: the issuing CA's database and key, the Group Policy set, the router's configuration, the log archive, and the living records each get their protected, cataloged copy.

stages.title: Carry the copies to the offline cabinet
stages.detail: A backup that sits on the server it protects fails with it. Move a copy of each backup to the offline cabinet by hand, under the same custody rules as any media crossing a boundary, and keep the custody record that proves it.

stages.title: Rehearse a real restore, in isolation
stages.detail: One restore, actually performed: a domain controller's system state brought back on the isolated segment, timed against the objective, verified against the directory — plus the small restore everyone will someday need, from the Recycle Bin.

stages.title: File the recovery record and close the path
stages.detail: The Build path ends the way it worked: owners, schedules, and evidence. The recovery record joins the living documents, the final scans snapshot the finished network, and the Body of Evidence is ready for the authorization courses to assemble.

outcomeSummary: Backups with custody, one real restore performed in isolation, and the evidence that you can come back.
